name: Plymouth Gawater

notes: Carefully investigates Sylan's claims by asking about the journal's provenance, dating, authorship, and prophetic content.
Recognizes the journal by reputation despite apparently never reading it.
Introduces the concept known as 'Mother's Prayer' as potentially connected to the journal.
Recognized the journal's significance after hearing Sylan's description.
Identified the repeated poem heard in the Stronghold as the Mother's Prayer (or Mother's Prophecy).
Displayed great interest in determining whether Gerk truly fulfills the prophecy.
Questioned Sylan about the journal's historical context, dates, and contents before drawing conclusions.
Explains the origins and significance of the Mother's Prayer.
States the Mother's Prayer is sacred to the Navi and historically identified heroes who aided Atlas.
Has personally encountered three previous sons or daughters of the Great Tree.
Reveals that one previous chosen accepted the calling while two rejected it.
States that roughly 1,500 years have passed since someone willingly accepted the role.
Explains that the Mother's Tales can change based on the choices of the chosen individual.
Explains the origin of the keystones.
Reveals the Navi created the keystones by studying and distilling the rings of the Eldarin Tree.
States that creating the keystones unintentionally began the Mother's Prayer.
Offers Gerk the ancient office of Doorman and explains its responsibilities.
Retrieves the Keystone of Pitel from the dais and presents it to Gerk.
Explains that the Eldarin Tree is the sacred origin of the keystones.
Reveals the Navi created the keystones by studying and distilling the rings of the Eldarin Tree.
Reveals that creating the keystones unintentionally began the Mother's Prayer prophecy.
Performs the formal ceremony appointing new Doormen.
Explains that previous keepers only preserved keystones while the new Doormen must actively protect and improve their assigned realms.
Personally presents the Midgar, Gilbrick, and La-rel keystones during the ceremony.
Conducts the formal ceremony assigning the remaining keystones to the party.
Explains that the previous keepers only hid and preserved the keystones while the new guardians are expected to actively protect and improve their assigned realms.
Allows each recipient the freedom to decline a keystone despite his recommendations.
Clarifies that Lith rejected conventional magic but has its own culture rooted in folklore and myths.
Assigns the remaining keystones to the party.
Explains that La-rel and Terov will remain under stewardship until future keepers are found.
Warns that the party must now protect the artifacts the lich seeks.
States he can guide the keepers but cannot dictate how they use the keystones.
Hints that becoming a keeper has fundamentally changed the party.
Completes the distribution of the keystones.
Explains that the party are now keystone keepers and honorary Children of the Great Eldarin Tree.
Clarifies that Gerk is the Doorman while the others are Gatekeepers.
Admits he only understands these powers through ancient tomes because no one has used them for centuries.
Warns that leaving major portals open is dangerous because hostile creatures have previously entered through them.
Plans to teach Gerk how to properly use and control the portal system.
Expresses interest in understanding Walker's apparent portal-travel abilities.

openQuestions: How does Plymouth know about the journal?
Who were the previous three sons or daughters of the Great Tree?
What changes come with becoming a keystone keeper?
How much does Plymouth truly know about the full capabilities of the keystones?
